test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Foundational Full Test - 03
subject: general
question: 5 men and 6 boys can complete the work in 10 days, the same amount of work done by 8 men and 14 boys in 5 days, then find the number of days required by 6 men and 5 boys to complete the same amount of work.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the total work using M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂:

(5m + 6b) × 10 = (8m + 14b) × 5

10m + 12b = 8m + 14b ⇒ 2m = 2b ⇒ m = b (efficiency of 1 man = 1 boy)

Total work = (5 + 6) × 10 = 110 units (since m = b = 1).

Days for (6 men + 5 boys) = 110 ÷ (6 + 5) = 110 ÷ 11 = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by (5 men + 6 boys) = 10 days

⇒ Time taken by (8 men + 14 boys) = 5 days

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 5 men + 6 boys
 10
 10
 1
 
 

 8 men + 14 boys
 5
 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of 1 man be m and 1 boy be b.

⇒ From the table, 5m + 6b = 1 — (Eq 1)

⇒ 8m + 14b = 2 — (Eq 2)

⇒ Multiply Eq 1 by 2: 10m + 12b = 2

⇒ Equating the efficiencies: 10m + 12b = 8m + 14b

⇒ 10m − 8m = 14b − 12b

⇒ 2m = 2b ⇒ m = b

⇒ Substitute m = b into Eq 1: 5m + 6m = 11m = 1

⇒ Efficiency of (6 men + 5 boys) = 6m + 5b = 11m

⇒ Since 11m = 1, their combined efficiency is 1 unit/day.

⇒ Required time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Required time = 10 ÷ 1 = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Equivalence Formula (MDH)

If M₁ persons can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours/day, then M₁D₁H₁ / W₁ = M₂D₂H₂ / W₂.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the amount of work done. If the time worked is constant, wages are distributed strictly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When workers operate on alternate days, find the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days) and use it to estimate the total number of complete cycles required before assessing the remaining work.
